text: I argued with authority figures.
I had verbal outbursts towards people or objects (e.g., yelling or rages).
I blamed others for my mistakes or misbehaviour.
I liked getting the attention of others, or being a person who gets noticed.
I stretched the truth or made things up to help me get what I wanted.
I was good at conning, tricking, or fooling other people.
I used people to get what I wanted.
I felt that I deserved special treatment.
I believed I was more important than other people.
I deliberately annoyed people.
I made promises that I didn't really intend to keep.
I disregarded or was unconcerned about the feelings of others.
I thought it wasn't a big deal if I hurt other people or their feelings.
I didn't react to things that seemed to make others emotional.
I was physically aggressive towards people, animals, or property.
I used more alcohol or other drugs than I had planned to, or for longer than I had planned to.
I kept using alcohol or other drugs even though it caused or worsened a problem with my mental or physical health.
I spent a lot of time acquiring, using, or recovering from the effects of alcohol or other drugs.
I needed more alcohol or other drugs to get the effect I wanted, or experienced less effect from the same amount.
I had a strong desire or urge to use alcohol or other drugs.
I kept using alcohol or other drugs even though it caused or worsened problems in my relationships.
I wanted to cut down on my use of alcohol or other drugs, or tried to and couldn't.
I used alcohol or other drugs to relieve or avoid withdrawal symptoms due to stopping use of alcohol or other drugs.
I used alcohol or other drugs where it was physically dangerous (e.g., I drove a car while impaired by alcohol or drugs).
I felt numbness or tingling in my body.
I experienced trembling or shaking.
I felt chills in my body.
Others seemed to think I was odd or unusual.
I had thoughts that made sense to me but that other people said were strange.
I felt unsteady.
I felt slowed down (e.g., thinking or moving slowly).
I suddenly felt as if someone else, or a different part of myself, took control of my perception of the world, thinking, emotions, or behaviour.
I suddenly felt as if I had the state of mind or memories of a different person, or of a different part of myself.
I couldn't remember an important part of a traumatic event I experienced.

There were gaps in my memory of everyday events or well-learned skills (e.g., I found unexplained objects in my belongings, others described things I had done that I didn't remember doing, or I temporarily lost access to skills I usually have).
I felt numb to physical pain or discomfort.
I had two or more distinct personalities.
I had an experience that most people would think is unusual (e.g., sensing the presence of someone who isn't actually there).
I saw, felt, or heard things that other people could not see, feel, or hear, while awake.
Other people removed thoughts from my head.
I could influence other people just by sending my thoughts to them.
I had a strong belief about something even though most people would have believed it was not true.

I felt a need to perform repetitive acts (e.g., checking, cleaning, counting, washing, praying, or repeating words silently) to deal with intrusive thoughts, images, or urges, to reduce my anxiety or distress, or to prevent something bad from happening.
I did not need as much sleep as usual.
I found it hard to use the right words to explain or describe a topic or a series of events, or to have a conversation.
I found it hard to think or concentrate.
I found it hard to pay attention.
I found it increasingly difficult to do more than one task at a time.
It took more effort than usual to organise and plan things, or to make decisions.
Tasks took me longer than they used to.
I failed to finish the tasks I was supposed to do (e.g., started tasks but quickly lost focus or was sidetracked).
I found it difficult to organise tasks and activities or manage my time.
